config.description:
The name of the instance's configuration (similar but not
quite the same as a region) which defines the geographic placement and
replication of your databases in this instance. It determines where your data
is stored. Values are typically of the form 'regional-europe-west1' , 'us-central' etc.
In order to obtain a valid list please consult the
[Configuration section of the docs](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/instances).
config.rationale: The config field determines where data is stored geographically. While it does not directly introduce a security risk, it should be set to a region that complies with data residency requirements.

default_backup_schedule_type.description:
Controls the default backup behavior for new databases within the instance.
Note that 'AUTOMATIC' is not permitted for free instances, as backups and backup schedules are not allowed for free instances.
if unset or NONE, no default backup schedule will be created for new databases within the instance. Possible values: ["NONE", "AUTOMATIC"]
default_backup_schedule_type.rationale: Setting a default backup schedule ensures new databases are automatically backed up, reducing the risk of data loss in the event of accidental deletion or corruption.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description:
The descriptive name for this instance as it appears in UIs. Must be
unique per project and between 4 and 30 characters in length.
display_name.rationale: The display name is a required identifier for the instance. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should follow naming conventions for clarity.

edition.description: The edition selected for this instance. Different editions provide different capabilities at different price points. Possible values: ["EDITION_UNSPECIFIED", "STANDARD", "ENTERPRISE", "ENTERPRISE_PLUS"]
edition.rationale: The edition affects available features and pricing but does not directly introduce a security risk.

force_destroy.description:
When deleting a spanner instance, this boolean option will delete all backups of this instance.
This must be set to true if you created a backup manually in the console.
force_destroy.rationale: Enabling force_destroy allows a Cloud Spanner instance to be destroyed even if it contains databases, risking permanent and irreversible data loss.

instance_type.description:
The type of this instance. The type can be used to distinguish product variants, that can affect aspects like:
usage restrictions, quotas and billing. Currently this is used to distinguish FREE_INSTANCE vs PROVISIONED instances.
When configured as FREE_INSTANCE, the field 'edition' should not be configured. Possible values: ["PROVISIONED", "FREE_INSTANCE"]
instance_type.rationale: The instance type affects available features and quotas but does not directly introduce a security risk.

labels.description:
An object containing a list of "key": value pairs.
Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are used for organisation and cost allocation. They do not directly introduce a security risk but can be used to enforce governance policies.

name.description:
A unique identifier for the instance, which cannot be changed after
the instance is created. The name must be between 6 and 30 characters
in length.
If not provided, a random string starting with 'tf-' will be selected.
name.rationale: The instance name is an optional identifier. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should follow naming conventions to avoid confusion.

num_nodes.description:
The number of nodes allocated to this instance. Exactly one of either num_nodes, processing_units or
autoscaling_config must be present in terraform except when instance_type = FREE_INSTANCE.
num_nodes.rationale: The number of nodes affects availability and performance but does not directly introduce a security risk.

processing_units.description:
The number of processing units allocated to this instance. Exactly one of either num_nodes,
processing_units or autoscaling_config must be present in terraform except when instance_type = FREE_INSTANCE.
processing_units.rationale: Processing units affect availability and performance but do not directly introduce a security risk.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project field is optional and defaults to the provider project. It does not directly introduce a security risk but should be explicitly set to avoid deploying resources to unintended projects.

autoscaling_config.description:
The autoscaling configuration. Autoscaling is enabled if this field is set.
Exactly one of either num_nodes, processing_units or autoscaling_config must be
present in terraform except when instance_type = FREE_INSTANCE.
When autoscaling is enabled, num_nodes and processing_units are treated as,
OUTPUT_ONLY fields and reflect the current compute capacity allocated to
the instance.

autoscaling_config.asymmetric_autoscalin.description: Asymmetric autoscaling options for specific replicas.

The target high priority cpu utilization percentage that the autoscaler
should be trying to achieve for this replica.
This number is on a scale from 0 (no utilization) to 100 (full utilization).

The target total cpu utilization percentage that the autoscaler
should be trying to achieve for this replica.
This number is on a scale from 0 (no utilization) to 100 (full utilization).

If true, disables high priority CPU autoscaling for this replica and ignores
high_priority_cpu_utilization_percent in the top-level autoscaling configuration.

If true, disables total CPU autoscaling for this replica and ignores
total_cpu_utilization_percent in the top-level autoscaling configuration.
The maximum number of nodes for this specific replica.

The maximum number of processing units for this specific replica.
If set, this number should be multiples of 1000 and be greater than or equal to
min_processing_units.
The minimum number of nodes for this specific replica.

The minimum number of processing units for this specific replica.
If set, this number should be multiples of 1000.
The location of the replica to apply asymmetric autoscaling options.
autoscaling_config.asymmetric_autoscalin.rationale: The replica location affects data residency but does not directly introduce a security risk on its own.

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_limits.description:
Defines scale in controls to reduce the risk of response latency
and outages due to abrupt scale-in events. Users can define the minimum and
maximum compute capacity allocated to the instance, and the autoscaler will
only scale within that range. Users can either use nodes or processing
units to specify the limits, but should use the same unit to set both the
min_limit and max_limit.

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_limits.ma.description:
Specifies maximum number of nodes allocated to the instance. If set, this number
should be greater than or equal to min_nodes.

Specifies maximum number of processing units allocated to the instance.
If set, this number should be multiples of 1000 and be greater than or equal to
min_processing_units.

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_limits.mi.description:
Specifies number of nodes allocated to the instance. If set, this number
should be greater than or equal to 1.

Specifies minimum number of processing units allocated to the instance.
If set, this number should be multiples of 1000.

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_targets.description:
Defines scale in controls to reduce the risk of response latency
and outages due to abrupt scale-in events

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_targets.h.description:
Specifies the target high priority cpu utilization percentage that the autoscaler
should be trying to achieve for the instance.
This number is on a scale from 0 (no utilization) to 100 (full utilization)..
autoscaling_config.autoscaling_targets.h.rationale: CPU utilization targets affect performance but do not directly introduce a security risk.

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_targets.s.description:
Specifies the target storage utilization percentage that the autoscaler
should be trying to achieve for the instance.
This number is on a scale from 0 (no utilization) to 100 (full utilization).
autoscaling_config.autoscaling_targets.s.rationale: Storage utilization targets affect performance but do not directly introduce a security risk.

autoscaling_config.autoscaling_targets.t.description:
The target total cpu utilization percentage that the autoscaler should be trying to achieve for the instance.
This number is on a scale from 0 (no utilization) to 100 (full utilization). The valid range is [10, 90] inclusive.
If not specified or set to 0, the autoscaler will skip scaling based on total cpu utilization.
The value should be higher than high_priority_cpu_utilization_percent if present.
